request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have an end date. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works now**
- **Storing and setting a rate:** a new `to_date` column (migration `V32__rate_to.sql`) holds the end date, and setting a rate saves it. If the to-date is before the from-date, the server refuses the request with an error. The rate form checks this too and shows `rate-form-error`. When a to-date is given, the `RATE_SET` audit line ends with `to=<date>`.
- **When a rate applies:** the server picks the rate with the latest from-date on or before the day, as before. If that rate's to-date is earlier than the day, there is no rate and due is n/a. Nothing else falls back to an older rate. All due figures go through this one lookup in `RateRepository.findInForce`, so person totals, sheet totals, rollup audit lines and the late charge all follow (n/a is skipped, and there's nothing to add a late charge to). The front end's copy of the lookup (`pctOn`) does the same, which also covers the "in force today" table. The rate form has a new To field (`rate-form-to`), and the rate list shows the end date in `rate-to`.
- **Statements:** this needed one more change. Before, a claim stated while it had no due stayed "live", so it picked up the next rate set later. The spec expects a claim that is n/a because its rate ended to stay n/a after a statement. So a statement now records that the claim is stated as n/a, in a new `stated_na` flag on claims (migration `V33__claim_stated_na.sql`). The server and front end both treat that claim's due as fixed at n/a.

**Decision for you:** I kept the old behaviour for claims dated before any rate existed: they still stay live after a statement. Only the ended-rate case is held at n/a, which matches how the request is worded. If you'd rather every n/a be fixed by a statement, it's a small change in `Dues.bindsNa`.

Setting a rate again for the same grade and from-date replaces its to-date, so leaving To blank removes an existing end date.
